title: Popes | Award Winning Short Film | British Comedy
description:
The Vatican goes online. The junior priests are not ready.

Subscribe to our YouTube channel ▶ https://www.youtube.com/@CenterFrame

Aided by a film crew, Father Richard Pope struggles through a welcome speech for the Vatican new Online Hub.

Later, Richard and his fellow priests, Father Michael and Father Cain, push on with dragging the Church into the 21st century. Michael fixation on The Da Vinci Code gets his internet access revoked, and his petition to canonise Luke Skywalker sends Richard over the edge. Cain, meanwhile, pitches moving an old pay-your-way-into-heaven scheme online and courting influencers, with crypto, NFTs and purgatory-bound souls to follow. It is enough to make Richard question Cain calling entirely.

Writer Mark Hammersley dreamed Popes up on an L.A. rooftop while touring The Last Confession, wondering who actually writes the Vatican spreadsheets. Directed by James Duffy of Pink Static Films and built as a proof of concept for a series, it takes its cues from The Thick of It, Silicon Valley, Rev and The Vicar of Dibley: an irreverent look at the world oldest institution trying to stay relevant.

Popes won Best Comedic Short Film at the All The Laughs Comedy Awards and Best Short Comedy at The White Rose International Film Festival, with finalist and official selection nods at Lit Laughs, Pigeon Laughs, New York City Short Comedy, LA Comedy and Greenwich.

A short film about faith, bureaucracy, and keeping the world oldest institution relevant.

Written by Mark Hammersley and directed by James Duffy.

title: RESET | AI Sci-Fi Short Film | Higgsfield Film Festival
description:
Every civilization believes it is the light. Every civilization has an enemy it calls the dark. Given the freedom to choose, the peoples of Earth have chosen the same thing in every age: not love, but dominion. Now the universe has answered — the planet will be returned to its beginning. On the Moon, the last two rulers of Earth meet to argue over a sentence that has already been passed: a queen of light and a king of fire, heirs to a war older than memory. 

Director’s statement:
I made RESET alone, with artificial intelligence as my crew. Every frame, every voice and every sound was generated — but the film was directed: the story, the shot list, the rhythm of every cut, the silence between the lines, the color of every image. I wanted to prove that an AI film can be quiet. That it can hold a frame, trust a face, and let two characters simply look at each other while a world ends behind them.

CREATED & EDITED BY — Max Barskih
COLOR CORRECTION — Kostiantyn Semerei

title: Classroom 2022 | IKLI Super Short Film Festival 2022
description:
CLASSROOM 2022 is a comedy-drama short film that follows a classroom election wherein students of Grade10 - Maharlika were tasked to appoint a new Class President for the school year. However, the majority of them failed to recall how important it is for everyone to take the election and voting process in a serious manner which led them to face certain consequences in the end.


In partnership with the Movement for Good Governance (MGG), YouthLed PH,YouthVote Philippines, and Rappler, Ticket2Me, the country’s leading independent creator monetization platform, pioneers again by launching IKLI: The Philippines' First Super Short FilmFestival.

Inspired by other microfilm festivals around the world, IKLI is an annual, online film festival initially featuring three categories - Micro short films, mini short films, and super short films with the festival motto,"The simpler, the better!"

For 2022, the theme is "Bitin! We deserve better!" to draw attention, in an entertaining but enlightening way, the many stories that can help convince Filipinos all over the world that we deserve better: better government, better healthcare, better education, better livelihoods, better transportation - even better love lives!

title: The Quarantined Ms. Meow | Short Film | Solanki Chakraborty
description:
Indian Film Festival Stuttgart , Stuttgart / Germany, 2021
GreyJo Online Short Film Festival selection / Best cinematography nomination, 2021
Festival RNAB , Sao Paulo / Brazil, 2021
Noble International Film Festival & Awards, Bangalore / India, 2021
Happy Valley Animation Festival (Finalist Best Experimental Animation),PA / USA,2021
Lift-off Global Network First -Time Filmmaker Sessions , Pinewood Studio / UK,2021

The Quarantined Ms. Meow is a stop motion homemade film made by all available household materials during the lockdown. As a filmmaker quarantine was an unpleasant experience. There was a certain degree of psychological distress in terms of–depression, anxiety, and stress during the strict 40 days of mandatory lockdown. This short film allowed me to showcase a perfect creative outlet to practice my craft as a budding filmmaker. Self-isolating at home, I thought it might be the right time to design a short film that I could execute with limited resources. And through this creative venture, I had attempted to hypothesize that quantification of the psychological impact of the current situation and serves as a critique to the policies and implementation strategies to cope up with the psychological distress of the quarantined population.

6) Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF)2020
7) New York Indian Film Festival 2020
8) Kashish Mumbai International Queer Film Festival 2020
9) Dharamashala International Film Festival (DIFF) 2020
10) Kala Ghoda Art Festival 2021Mumbai as part of best of Kashish Film Festival

People who can’t be moulded into the stereotypes that society has set, often find it difficult
to make a place for themselves in the same society.
Hailing from a small town in India, Artika believes herself to be modern, liberal and most
importantly, independent. Not the one who shies away from speaking her mind. She
struggles to find a place to stay in Mumbai, overcoming the clichéd remarks of being a
“single working girl living alone”. However, an unprecedented encounter with a transgender
sex worker opposite her house, questions her beliefs. Will she now fall into the same
societal prejudices that she has been fighting against?

title: Prem Patra | Two lovers from the past. One girl from the present. A secret story | Hindi Short Film
description:
In 1970s India, Sakshi, a curious college girl, stumbles upon a hidden envelope under a garden bench while searching for a dropped coin. Inside is a nameless, heartfelt love letter. Drawn in by its mystery, Sakshi returns the next day—only to find a new letter, this time from the lover’s other half.

What begins as a fleeting curiosity becomes a quiet obsession, as Sakshi discovers an untold romance between two people separated by caste and family expectations. When their letter exchange abruptly ends, Sakshi, desperate to see love triumph, writes a reply pretending to be the man. But the woman senses the lie—his scent is missing—and in heartbreak, tears the letter away.

Left in disappointment, Sakshi returns once more—only to find a young man with a plastered leg searching under the same bench. Is he the one from the letters? Or just another coincidence?

title: Her-Story | LGBT Documentary Film | Nairita Thakurata, Sreecheta Das | Hook Films
description:
Her-Story is a short documentary film made using medium of live action film making and animation to paint the lives of two Trans-women of the Indian LGBT community, Atri and Pinot. Atri is a pragmatic Trans-woman and the first to appear for Civil service examination under the category of Transgender in India. She has achieved this after a long fight to make her identity recognisable before India. Pinot on the other hand is coming out colourfully before the world as a proud Trans-woman full of optimistic dreams. Through the sources of the LGBT community and this documentary film, Atri and Pinot befriended each other while fighting the battle of making their identity known.

title: Atonement | Bengali Short Film | Surajit Kundu | Hook Films
description:
Short film about two childhood friends who meet after very long time but at an abnormal situation. One of them recognises the other, but the other one cannot, may be because of his daily stressful and hectic lifestyle. Their school days depict a story of their strong bond of friendship. During their class 10th selection exams one of them did not show his answer script to the other to cheat, and because of which the other friend did not get through his board exams. Eventually stopping him to study further.
The night when they met at an abnormal situation, the tyrant recognising his friend tries to plant a sweet revenge on the other. We call it Revenge; let's see why they call it ATONEMENT.

title: Checkmate | Bengali Short Film | Rudradev Bhattacharya | Hook Films
description:
The plot for this short film revolves around the euphoric chess game between the alter ego of an individual. Amidst the hustling city, a man couches back with his memories on his chair and puts his failures and regrets on a game of chess. Checkmate is the story of every person who has wanted the social order to change in their favour but couldn’t. This is all about people who have dreamt of a better society but just severely failed at not getting the desired returns.
What does he conclude on the chess game in rendezvous with his alter ego? There resides another person, another mind within us, all of us. It is on us to let them parasite on us or let us parasite on them. Welcome all to the world of your own self. Your own alter ego, that resides within you.

Set in a serene coastal village of Maharashtra, Prawns is an emotional and inspiring story of a widowed fisherman and his 10-year-old son. title: KAMUKI (SWEETHEART)  - NATIONAL AWARD WINNING SHORT FILM - SRFTI
description:
Winner of several awards including the Swarna Kamal(Golden Lotus) for Best Direction in Non-feature section at the 63rd National Film Awards, Kamuki (Sweetheart) tells the story of Divya, a 17-year-old feisty school girl. When Divya discovers that she is pregnant, nothing can stop her from tracking down her estranged boyfriend and claiming him back into her life. 

The film has been screened in international film festivals in Toronto, Los Angeles, Warsaw, Bialystok, Ottawa, Rajshahi, Goa, Mumbai, Delhi among others. 

“A sensitive portrayal of a young woman’s determination to uphold her dignity against all odds” – National Film Award Citation

“Delicate emotions are examined with impeccable precision in this intimate and nuanced exploration of the ephemeral nature of young love and its mighty illusions that are forces to be reckoned with.” – Indian Film Festival Of Los Angeles (IFFLA) 

“For its intimate portrayal of the upheaval in a teenage girl’s universe and her discovery of the strength and resolve within” – Official Jury of Signs 2016

“For handling a very contemporary issue in a realistic manner” – The Jury for Malayalam Documentary and Short Fiction Film of Federation of Film Societies of India (FFSI) FFSI

title: AlpViraam | A Neo-Parallel Film
description:
|MADE FOR BLUETOOTH DEVICES|

Sanjeev Pathak has won a Sahitya Akademi award for his first novel, Main Nahin Hun. His first, international-bestselling book has won hearts because of it sadhesion to the roots. It is reminiscent of Madhubani paintings and whatever one has left behind, in life. It has taken Hindi literature to a different, next level. Like Geetanjali's Tomb of Sand did. However, it will have been six years, from now, that Sanjeev wouldn't write a word. He wouldn't be inspired at all. Why?

A journalist, RK wonders why a writer has stopped all of a sudden. Why he has become Ek Ruka Hua Lekhak. Doesn't an award, the highest for literature, push one enough to write whatever he wishes to? To find out, he sets out to meet Sanjeev. It's an afternoon when he's gotten an appointment or an opportunity to ask him what he might answer. It's an ordinary home, away from home, in Mumbai. A writer's home. RK chooses not to bomb his questions in the very beginning, but, to listen.

Sanjeev tells him what life had been, has become and might turn out to be. It's only after he shows RK, a college-time photograph, that he understands that it is a company that Sanjeev is missing in life. It also reminds him of a phrase he had read in the book. Push & Pull theory. When he asks to elaborate, Sanjeev tells what pulls him back but is reluctant to tell him what pushes him. Or maybe, he doesn't know. Maybe, he will, once he is done being fixated on the huge photograph of an old man, on the wall behind RK. Or once he has brewed coffee for both of 'em. Or maybe, he will tell a different story.

title: Goodnight Giggles | Short Film | Nirmal Joshi
description:
Garima (Giggles), a young physician, and Shashank (Shanks) a young IT professional, living in Philadelphia, enjoy a spousal relationship in bed that is marked by witty and funny verbal exchanges surrounding their sexual encounters. This results from intimacy conflicts between an inherently more risk-taking male partner and a fiercely independent female partner. The film focuses on two phases of their lives in bed (late twenties and mid-forties) to have the viewer witness the funny sexual banter. After a group of male friends take Shanks out to a strip club for his 45th birthday, the inherently trusting Giggles suspects that he has played out a forbidden fantasy with one of the dancers. Giggles, egged on by a female friend, decides to trap Shanks into confessing ….and waits eagerly to see the result.

title: Alexa | Short Film | Ft. Rupali Rahul, Asif Husain | By Kaustubh Sawant
description:
Daksh Anand and Alisha Chauhan are in love and have decided to move in together in their new house. Alisha a strong headed independent woman has decided to take the responsibility of picking the perfect house for them, while Daksh is in a different city travelling to Mumbai, to move in with Alisha. 

Everything looks beautiful and perfect, Daksh is supportive, Alisha is open and vulnerable with Daksh. Daksh is introduced to Alexa an electronic device that belongs to Alisha. Daksh and Alisha set up the house according to their liking. It’s a dream like world for them. But as time passes, Daksh starts getting comfortable. Alisha starts noticing certain details about Daksh, which may seem minor but are very problematic. 

Alisha looks for support in her friend Rashida, as the relationship between Daksh and Alisha has reached rough waters very soon. One fine night Alisha sees a glimpse of Daksh’s dark truth. What happens next ? Does Alisha see the dark side of Daksh crystal clear? Or falls prey to Daksh’s tactics.

title: A Tale of Two Indians | Short Film | Raghav Parmar
description:
Aman and Arif, friends from different religious backgrounds, come together to celebrate Independence Day. They engage in the joy of flying a kite, but their playful moment takes an unexpected turn when they face a challenge: they must save an egg from falling down. In their determined efforts to save the fragile life, a parallel world unfolds where a communal riot erupts between the two communities, resulting in violence and bloodshed. However, as the narrative unfolds, the fate of the egg becomes intertwined with the tragic tale of these two Indian friends.

title: Kasak | Short Film | Mitisha Gupta & Udayan Koshal | by Kayomarz Daruwala
description:
Kasak intimately explores the deep bond of love that envelopes a man and a woman. 
Their connection is a symphony of shared experiences, a mosaic of emotions, and a profound understanding that transcends words.

It's a dance of two souls, intricately choreographed by fate, where they move together in harmony through the highs and lows of existence. Their laughter is a soothing melody, and their touch, an electric current of affection that courses through their veins.

This bond serves as a refuge, a sanctuary where they find solace in each other's presence. In the warmth of their embrace, they discover strength, comfort, and a sense of belonging, which is unique. In the grand tapestry of life, their bond is a golden thread, weaving a narrative of love, resilience, and the enduring power of human connection, a timeless story that bears witness to the beauty of their intertwined souls.

title: The Elephant In the Room | Daisy Shah | Nitinn R Miranni | Viraf Patell | Salonie.P | Krishan Hooda
description:
Nitinn and Meher have been dating for 1.5 yrs. and Nitinn is ready to pop THE question, Meher is a bit iffy about them. Excitement and the preparations are in full swing for their first Ganpati, “Gannu”, together but this guest might be more than what they had wished for. Meher forms an uncanny connection with Gannu when he starts talking to her and spilling her guests' secrets. Meher is unable to keep the secrets to herself and everyone comes under the microscope.

The past is presented in a new light, testing the old and new relationships alike. None of her guests are spared from the past lies, jealousy or love triangles. Relationships are on trial and they are losing track of who likes who and who has slept with whom.

They fight out this war of secrets, each hoping to lose. In the end, all they are left with are a bunch of truths and a question, whether they should pray for what they need vs what they want in life.

title: Julieta x Julieta | Curta-Metragem Premiado | Filme de Aline Carválho
description:
Julieta x Julieta foi exibido em 10 festivais nacionais e internacionais, com seleções oficiais no Brasil, Índia, Itália, Reino Unido e Estados Unidos.

🏆 RECONHECIMENTOS E PREMIAÇÕES

Julieta x Julieta conquistou importantes reconhecimentos em festivais nacionais e internacionais:

• 🏆 Vencedor da Menção Honrosa no Festival del Cinema di Cefalù, na Itália. 🇮🇹

• 🏆 Vencedor de Melhor Filme LGBT no Take Único – Minas Gerais, Brasil. 🇧🇷

• 🏆 Vencedor do Prêmio Aclamação do Público na 4ª Mostra FAMA de Cinema, em Minas Gerais, Brasil. 🇧🇷

• ⭐ Finalista no Lift-Off Global Network Sessions, no Reino Unido. 🇬🇧

O filme integrou a programação do renomado Kalakari Film Fest, na Índia, um festival reconhecido por unir cinema e impacto social, promovendo iniciativas humanitárias e ações voltadas ao apoio de pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, incluindo campanhas de distribuição de alimentos para pessoas em situação de rua.

A obra também ganhou destaque internacional ao ter sua trajetória registrada em um livro publicado na Itália, com sua biografia completa apresentada em italiano, ampliando o reconhecimento da produção no cenário cultural europeu. A publicação teve circulação comercial pela Amazon, levando a história do filme e de sua criação a novos públicos.

🎬 SINOPSE

Em meio ao caos da maior metrópole do país, duas mulheres de personalidades e trajetórias completamente diferentes se encontram por obra do destino.

Julieta x Julieta é um curta-metragem brasileiro dirigido por Aline Carválho que acompanha o encontro de duas mulheres fortes, com histórias e visões de mundo distintas. Em meio a conflitos, descobertas e escolhas inesperadas, elas vivem minutos intensos marcados por surpresas, reviravoltas e pela força de seus próprios instintos.


🎥 FICHA TÉCNICA

title: RUBY – ein Kurzfilm
description:
// ENGLISH VERSION AVAILABLE:
// https://youtu.be/IiavLUfbmgM

Ruby ist eine Außenseiterin in der Schule - aber ein absolutes Technik-Genie, mit dem Hang dazu, Türen mit der Aufschrift "Betreten Verboten" zu öffnen.

Ein Kurzfilm von zugdirekt.

Die englische Version: https://youtu.be/IiavLUfbmgM


RUBY Gewinnt bei dem Festival "Flimmern & Rauschen 2017" den Münchner Jugendfilmpreis in der Kategorie der 17 bis 21 Jährigen.

Der Außenseiterin Ruby sind „Computer lieber als Menschen“ Sie mag ihr Dasein als Nerd und dass sie von allen in Ruhe gelassen wird. Als sie die Gelegenheit bekommt, sich in die Handys ihrer Mitschüler einzuhacken, nutzt sie das gnadenlos aus und bringt Beziehungen und Freundschaften total durcheinander. Der unter Leitung von Amon Ritz von 17 Schülerinnen und Schülern des Albert-Einstein-Gymnasiums in eigenverantwortlicher Arbeit entstandene Kurzspielfilm RUBY zeichnet ein facettenreiches Bild eines Mädchens, das sich an ihr Außenseiterdasein gewöhnt hat und nun plötzlich das Leben anderer bestimmen kann. Bewusst wird dabei nicht die Moralkeule geschwungen. Dank der tollen und sehr eigenen Bildsprache, der guten Darsteller und nicht zuletzt der passenden Musik ist RUBY ein überaus gelungener Film, der einen Preis mehr als verdient hat.

RUBY ist nominiert für das Bayrische Kinder & Jugend Filmfestival 2018 in Roth.



Laudatio der Jury der 39. Filmtagen der bayerischen Schulen:

Sie ist echt anders drauf: steht auf Programmieren, Schrauben und Löten. Klar, dass außer dem Klassen-Nerd keiner viel mit ihr zu tun haben will. Nur wenn mal das Smartphone zickt, kann man sie gebrauchen. Doch Ruby sollte keiner unterschätzen. Sie schreibt ihren eigenen Code und hackt sich nach und nach in die Smartphones der „supercoolen“ Mitschüler ein. Jede noch so intime Message liest sie mit und beginnt schon nach kurzer Zeit, Gott zu spielen. Delikate Clips werden gepostet, Beziehungen gehen in die Brüche, keiner traut mehr dem anderen, alles gerät ins Rutschen. Nur Ruby hängt mitten drin fest auf der Rutsche ihres Lebens.
In unglaublich eindringlichen Bildern erzählen die Filmemacher die vielschichtige Story des hochbegabten Mädchens, das sich am Ende in seiner Zerstörungslust findet. Herausragendes Schauspiel, technische Perfektion und eine professionelle filmische Haltung lassen nur eine Diagnose zu: schwer preisverdächtig.

Die Filmgruppe erhält den Förderpreis des Staatsminister für Bildung und Kultus, Wissenschaft und Kunst, Dr. Ludwig Spaenle.






["Kapitel 0"]

Aufstehen.
Frühstück.

Selbstdiagnose: Außenseiter. Alternativ auch Nerd.
Computer sind mir lieber als Menschen.

"Ruby"

Mich lassen immer alle in Ruhe.
Auch die Lehrer.

"Kapitel 1"

Vor ein paar Wochen geschah etwas ungewöhnliches.
Dieser Junge gab mir sein Handy.
Ich sollte es reparieren.

Alles lief nach Plan
Bis ich versuchte das Backup einzuspielen.  
Um das Problem zu beheben, schrieb ich meine eigene Software. 
Es war wie eine unbeobachtete Tür mit der Aufschrift "Betreten Verboten", die einen Spalt offen stand.

"Kapitel 2"

Ich begann seine Nachrichten mitzulesen.
Doch nach einer Zeit wurde das Langweilig.

Doch ich begann es zu übertreiben.

"Kapitel 3"

Mit einem Klick konnte ich Beziehungen und Freundschaften zerstören.

"Kapitel 4"

Mir ging es einfach beschissen.
Ich wusste das ich zu weit gegangen war.
Immer öfter hatte ich Alpträume.

Selbstdiagnose Außenseiter.
Doch jetzt weiß ich genau wer ich bin.
Und ich würde es jederzeit wieder tun.

title: LA VALIGIA || Stop Motion Short Film
description:
An old man is sitting on the edge of a bed in a bare room with stoned walls, his face furrowed with deep wrinkles and his unkempt beard, gnarled hands still full of life, curved shoulders: he is alone and thoughtful. A small and ramshackle window with bars is the only outlet to the outside. In front of him he has a mysterious suitcase. Opening it the man finds himself in his hands the photographs and the personal effects of a whole life. Thus begins the sequence of memories and visions, synapses of the mind that come to life and invade the room of the elderly bringing him back in time, first adult then boy, finally child.

title: SIRI MIRI - سرّي مرّي | Palestinian Short Film
description:
Siri Miri is an award-winning Palestinian short film set in the occupied West Bank that satirically captures the life of Palestinian youth living in a technological age and no-so-helpful AI assistants. Sick of their routine-run life spent coffee-sipping in smoke-filled coffeehouses, two teenagers turn to the help of Siri to no avail. This short film explores how the occupation affects every aspect of Palestinian life, including access to electricity and water, and a lack of freedom of movement.

سرّي مرّي هو فيلم قصير يعكس الواقع الفريد للحياة الفلسطينية تحت الاحتلال في الضفة الغربية المحتلة، حيث يعيش الشباب في عصر تكنولوجيا متقدمة. يلجأ اثنان من المراهقين إلى استخدام مساعد "سيري" دون أن يجدوا فائدة. يقوم هذا الفيلم القصير بتفحص كيف يؤثر الاحتلال على كافة جوانب الحياة الفلسطينية، بما في ذلك الوصول إلى الكهرباء والماء، ونقص حرية الحركة

title: Award Winning South African Short Film About Facing Your Past | WELCOME
description:
Welcome is an Award Winning South African Short Film About Facing Your Past.

James, a washed up South African writer needs to return to the home, he and his brother Ezekiel grew up in and he ran away from. Upon returning to the home the dark mysteries of the now empty house begin to reveal themselves again and James becomes haunted by the past he shares with the house and more importantly his now deceased father. A mysterious child, an ominous door and a broken home; James is faced with two choices run away again or confront his past. 

The Award Winning South African narrative of Welcome deals with something I believe we all can in someways relate to and that is the past we share with the home we grew up in. In many ways our home is symbolic of the person we have become or the person we never want to be and this narrative addresses both those sides; the good and the bad.

Subscribe for more of my filmmaker's perspective on life and (hopefully) growth inspiring content. 

Cheers!

title: Gunta | Short Film | Tejas Sonawane | Ft. Ashish Verma, Rajshri Deshpande, Gurpreet Sandhu
description:
Gunta is a look at the thorny relationship between a struggling young filmmaker Rahi (27) and his full-time house help Gurpreet (22) 

In India, it is common for the middle and upper classes to hire domestic helps to do regular household work. Often, these men and women come from small towns to big cities with enormous aspirations. 

Unfortunately, the exorbitant cost of living in cities like Mumbai, which has some of the highest real estate prices in the world and the lack of any formal education forces them to take up whatever work they can find. 

In a culture where dignity of labour is largely non-existent, one would imagine this would create tremendous social tension. However, while India’s rigid and highly stratified social structures help keep this house of cards from toppling over, these differences find other ways to manifest. 

Gunta is the story of two such individuals on opposite sides of the class divide, making an attempt to showcase their human sides and depicting the mundaneness and reality of everyday life in urban India.

title: Uss Mod Par | A bench in Mumbai becomes the eternal keeper of Niyati’s love, and unfulfilled dreams.
description:
Niyati, a 24-year-old from Lucknow, flees to Mumbai with her lover Vikas, chasing freedom and a new beginning. At a dimly lit bus depot, love and fear intertwine as they dream of a future away from family pressures. But in one cruel twist of fate, everything shatters—leaving only a bench, once a witness to promises, now a monument to loss. Years later, while life moves on, Niyati keeps returning to that bench, clinging not to closure, but to the haunting echo of what might have been.

https://www.buymeacoffee.com/miameowhttps://www.buymeacoffee.com/friendships

Director's Statement:
In the isolating times of the Covid-19 pandemic, I reflected on the nature of friendships – the ones that are fleeting, and those rare, enduring ones that withstand the test of time. This contemplation led to the realization that while not all friendships last, the ones that do are invaluable. "Friendship" is a tribute to these lasting connections.

The film, drawing from my personal experiences, narrates the story of two women from diverse backgrounds who meet in high school. Their journey through life, despite diverging paths due to family and career, is a testament to the enduring nature of their bond, surviving life's highs and lows.

"Friendship" aims to celebrate the beauty of reconnection, evoking nostalgia and encouraging viewers to rekindle their own meaningful friendships. It highlights the importance of human bonds in preventing the loneliness and depression often associated with isolation, underscoring the idea that connection is essential to our well-being.

Awards:
"Friendship" has not only resonated with audiences but also garnered critical acclaim, receiving over 25 selections at prestigious national and international film festivals. This widespread recognition reflects the film's universal appeal and its profound message. Among its accolades, the film won an IndieFEST Film Award, placing it alongside other high-profile winners, including the 2021 Academy Award-winning "If Anything Happens I Love You." It was also nominated for the Montreal Independent Film Festival, a distinguished event that draws Cannes award winners, Oscar nominees, and innovative independent films. These awards highlight the film's exceptional storytelling, artistic merit, and its significant impact on both critics and viewers, solidifying its place as a notable work in the realm of short films.

title: The Final Birthday - A vengeful spirit finds compassion through a lonely drunk man | Tamil
description:
After dying in a tragic accident caused by a drunk driver, a vengeful spirit haunts those who drown themselves in alcohol. One night, she targets a lonely young man celebrating his birthday in drunken despair. But as she shadows him, ready to strike, his childlike innocence, hidden grief, and honest remorse begin to disarm her fury. Through his vulnerable confessions of guilt and longing for love, the spirit feels something she thought she had lost forever compassion. Their strange, haunting bond builds toward a heartbreaking yet tender climax, where vengeance gives way to empathy, ending with her final words: “I am there for you.”

The festival gave us 14 winners, but we saw talent across so many entries. Today we're announcing Higgsfield Talent, a community program where we're investing more than $1,000,000 on top of the festival prizes to back more creators.

title: SOMETIME, SOMEWHERE | AI Sci-Fi Short Film | Higgsfield Global Film Festival #higgsfieldai
description:
Two machines were sent to find humanity a future. They found it 87,000 years after humanity ran out of time. @HiggsfieldAI 

SOMETIME, SOMEWHERE is a bittersweet science-fiction short about Pluto and Maxim — rival exploration robots built by competing Big Tech empires and sent into deep space to search for a world humanity could call home.

Their crews are gone. Earth has fallen silent. But the mission never ended, so they keep searching.

And eventually, impossibly, they succeed.

The tragedy isn’t that they fail. The tragedy is that they succeed too late.

SOMETIME, SOMEWHERE is my entry for the Higgsfield Global Film Festival.

Written and directed by Narottama Panitz. Every frame was generated in Higgsfield Cinema Studio.

title: Carbon Monoxide | Short Film | Rahul Yadav
description:
2nd Best Science Film Award(International Science Film Festival of India), Winner ( New Jersey India International Film Festival)
Winner (Veracruz Short International Film Festival)
Winner (Barcelona Planet Film Festival)
Winner (Cine Shorts International Film Festival)
Miami Independent Film Festival (Florida)
The Lift-Off Sessions (United Kingdom) 
Mumbai International Film Festival(MIFF-2020)
Winner-Cafe Irani Chai International Film Festival 2020

Carbon monoxide also known as silent killer, it is one of the deadliest combinations of gases that can kill people within minutes without even showing any physical symptoms. When we talk about air pollution, this gas remains least talked about but on the other hand causes highest number of deaths as compared to other gases. 
As per the data from various sources, most of the deaths happen when household fumes are generated either while cooking or in an attempt to warm houses in winters.
This film is the story of a master who keeps nine paying guest in his house as his extra source of income. One day, he left for outstation with his preacher ‘GURU’ for some work. When he come’s back he witnesses that all the paying guests were dead. The cause inhaling poisonous carbon monoxide gas. The gas was formed from a makeshift coal tandoor they improvised to party in their master’s absence without even thinking of the repercussions they could face.

title: Happy Teacher's Day | Sameer Sharma | Ft. Raghubir Yadav - Nominated For Filmfare 2022
description:
https://www.filmfare.com/awards/short-films-2022/finalists/masterji/4047

Who would have guessed that the world as we knew it would be altered because of a virus.
Lives changed overnight for everyone and our teachers were among those who were affected the most! 
Businesses turned to online sites, offices turned to work from home, and schools and colleges in their bid to adapt to the "new normal", turned to online education. 

Today when most students are equipped with technological devices, our teachers still continue to struggle and teach themselves, to unlearn the older ways of teaching, to learn to use technology they are completely unfamiliar with, and relearn their passion for teaching, even in the face of these difficulties, so that learning never stops. 

This short film is a tribute to celebrate their spirit to  Learn Unlearn Relearn
Here's to all the teachers who keep the world moving and growing everyday, who teach us to Keep Learning everyday.

title: Palayan - Broken homes and abandoned fields | Heart touching short drama - Hindi
description:
When Devansh, a young professional from Delhi, returns to his ancestral village in the mountains of Uttarakhand, he discovers more than just broken homes and abandoned fields he confronts the slow erasure of a once-vibrant world. Through fading memories, deserted schools, and heartfelt conversations with the few who remain, Palayan captures the emotional and cultural cost of migration from India’s Himalayan villages. Inspired by real stories, the film is a poetic meditation on home, loss, and the haunting ache of belonging not just to a place, but to a vanishing way of life.

title: Mazhabi Laddu | Children's Day Special | Award Winning Short Film | SSaurabh Tyagi
description:
Winner Best Picture - 5th Woodpecker International Film Festival
Official Selection - Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF), 2018
Official Selection - 8th Jagran Film Festival, 2017

This is a charming  story of a child called Azeem. He has innocent ideas and dreams. The film unfolds in a typical small town of U.P. Young Azeem lives with his sister and parents surrounded by noisy neighbours, naughty friends, busy shop-keepers, greedy goats, mischievous monkeys, fairs, mosques and temples. His father works as a halwai in a sweetmeat shop and Azeem loves to hang around there. His mother likes to fuss over him overly whilst she trains his sister to keep house. His friends like to play and roam around in old monuments and open pastures. All in all – an idyllic life.
Azeem loves the sweets prepared in his father’s shop specially the laddoos but the owner keeps an eagle eye. Moreover the laddoos are made for ‘prasad’ which is purchased by devotees as offerings to their Gods. Azeem and his friends attmept to partake of the prized laddoos even as they fear that heavens may fall if they actually do. It is a an enticing tale of friendship with a Goat called Salim and a friend called Ikram.  The fearful biases of elders and curiosity of little children. Innocence wins over differences. We are restrained by religious tenets yet we yearn for and seek to know the ‘other’. For together we rise..

title: Fear of God | Short Film | Siddhant Raj Singh | Abhishek Nishchal
description:
“When the eagles are silent, the parrots begin to jabber. The eagles —encounter
specialists—have been silent for far too long. The parrots, or the criminals, have not only
begun jabbering but are also flying without fear.” – J Dey

Fear of God brings attention to the reemerging underworld, who were rendered ineffective by the encounter specialists in the past, but are now creeping back into the mainstream.
A journalist is interviewing a retired Police commissioner of Mumbai, who was in service during the active years of Mumbai underworld, about the murder of an investigative journalist in broad daylight. The retired Police commissioner speaks about the presence of encounter specialists, during his time, who suppressed the underworld crimes with their effective and quick response. However, unlike in the past, the underworld is now operative in mainstream businesses,
but their way of operation is still illegal and dangerous. Hence he hints that it is about time that the encounter specialists are reinstated to uproot the underworld.

During the course of the interview, we intercut to show the modus operandi of the encounter specialists during 1998-2002 and the present challenges in tackling the underworld in the absence of the encounter specialist.

title: Jeyra: The Interrogation | World’s First Bengali AI Short Film
description:
Jeyra: The Interrogation is the world’s first Bengali AI psychological short film, set entirely inside a Kolkata police interrogation room. This dialogue-driven cinematic work explores power, silence, moral ambiguity, and human judgment through disciplined, realistic AI-assisted filmmaking.

Unlike many AI-generated films that rely on spectacle, fantasy, or heightened visuals, Jeyra deliberately embraces restraint. The film focuses on emotional realism, psychological nuance, and controlled performances—areas that demand precision, continuity, and subtle human behavior rather than visual excess.

The story unfolds in real time through conversation alone. What begins as routine questioning slowly transforms into a psychological confrontation, where authority, language, and personal bias shape an irreversible outcome. The confined space becomes a pressure chamber for human behavior, allowing tension and emotion to emerge organically through silence, pauses, and measured dialogue.

Produced using Google Flow for narrative and scene orchestration and Veo 3 for cinematic visual generation, the film demonstrates how generative AI can support disciplined, realistic filmmaking without overpowering storytelling intent. The technology remains deliberately invisible—serving the narrative rather than defining it.

As an early milestone in Bengali AI cinema, Jeyra: The Interrogation illustrates how artificial intelligence can coexist with traditional narrative structure, performance-driven writing, and minimal cinematic environments. It stands as a focused exploration of realism and cultural authenticity within AI-assisted storytelling.

title: Ijjat Ghar (The House of Dignity) | Short Documentary Film | Amar Fauzdar | Hook Films
description:
The basic needs for survival is health and hygiene, food and shelter. But the question is " Are these basic needs savoured by all the citizens of our nation?". Health and hygiene being foremost, Open defecation in various parts of India causing a series of illness. Over the past decade, a series of health campaigns being held in various parts of India promoting safe and healthy sanitary conditions. But joint initiative is what brings a positive outcome.
'इज़्जत घर (The House of Dignity)’ speaks about the recent breakthrough wherein the entire village of “Shahed Ghadi” in Uttar Pradesh with their joint initiative with Government owing to healthy sanitary conditions adopted to the toilet based defecation which serves to be a huge inspiration for various villages across India. They refer their toilets as “the house of dignity” owing to the importance of safe sanitary conditions. A proper sanitary facility is a symbol for positive growth of a nation.

title: Short Film  || PRANTIK --The cornered(Short Film)Directed by Subhasis Das
description:
I conceived the idea to do my work about the most cornered human’s of our society (At least in India) known as “Hijra” – Unaque or as Transgender. 
Here in our society they pay a visit to the houses when there is a new born; as it is believed that their blessings are auspicious & purest. 
And also in Indian mythology they have been appeared and used by others time to time. Even lord Arjuna camouflaged himself as a transgender during the end years of his exile and he was then known as ‘BRIHANNALA’. But society has always rejected these “BRIHANNALA’s” from the mainstream life and hence they were cornered over years after years--Director

title: Short Film White Noise| International Award Winning Short Film | Critically Acclaimed
description:
WHITE NOISE. Corpses of reality trudge on through this arid world. Yet my mind carries on with the expectation of a better, brighter earth. Awaiting the last verdant shower to cleanse the rough patches gives birth to my hope of clear dawn...the wait has continued through eons...still I rise with the conviction of a fresh dawn, of life arising from the pit of this coffin someday.

This film is based on a poem - "Escapist". Here four seasons of an entity are visually described in a symbolic way. Her emergence, participation in earthly emotion, contradiction with her ego, and dissolution-these four parts are shown in a surreal manner.

title: Louis' Shoes | Award-Winning CG Animated Short Film
description:
Louis, 8-and-a-half years old, is autistic. He arrives at his new school and is about to introduce himself.

A selection of Short of the Week, the web's leading curators of quality short films.

SUBMIT A FILM: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/submit/
FULL REVIEW: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/2021/11/11/louis-shoes/

Subscribe to S/W on YouTube!
Website: http://www.shortoftheweek.com
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ShortoftheWeek
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/shortoftheweek
Twitter: https://twitter.com/shortoftheweek

Les Chaussures de Louis
Directed by : Marion Philippe, Ka Yu Leung, Jean-Géraud Blanc, Théo Jamin
https://www.louis-shoes-film.com/

"Empathy can feel in short supply in today’s world, but the ability to place yourself in someone else’s shoes is an important skill when it comes to understanding others. If it isn’t something you possess in your toolkit, you might need a little help and film (and storytelling in general) is a great aid in eliciting such reactions. Les Chaussures de Louis (Louis’ Shoes) is a short looking to do just that, as it tells its story through the eyes of a young autistic boy in the hope of raising awareness and resonating with viewers.

Created at Ecole MoPA, by Jean-Géraud Blanc, Théo Jamin, Ka Yu Leung and Marion Philippe, the five-minute animation focuses on eight-and-a-half-year-old Louis on his first day at a new school. Asked to introduce himself to his new classmates, this is an important moment for the titular protagonist of Louis’ Shoes, as he wants them to understand his unique perspective of the world. Confused by the ritual of waving to say hello and with an aversion to eye contact, will his fellow pupils accept Louis for who he is? Or will they shun him and his blue, size 33 shoes?

Initially inspired by autistic philosophers, the quartet behind Louis’ Shoes recognised that for their film to be successful and genuine, pre-production was going to play an essential role and so they set out on what they describe as “a journey of interviews and research”. Basing their character and his experiences around the testimonials of people with autism, the team were able to create a sense of authenticity throughout their short and this, in turn, helps with the feeling of warmth and understanding that radiates from their story.

“Throughout the film, we thrive to create Louis’ particular way of seeing the world, which is at the same time a way of seeing ourselves, by walking, together, in his shoes”, the four co-directors explain. “The theme is specific but the struggle is universal. When the audience sees how Louis overcomes his difficulties with courage and sincerity, hopefully, it can resonate with people … even those without autism, to have the courage to accept and understand”.

Recognising CG animation as “the best tool” to do justice to the inspiring stories of their interviewees, Louis’ Shoes pairs its moving storyline with an affable aesthetic that welcomes its audience into Louis’ world. With the majority of the supporting characters framed so we never see their faces (until the very last scene), the team do a good job of inserting viewers in the gaze-avoiding point-of-view of their young protagonist. For some, this approach could have been limiting, but if anything it has forced this young team of animators to really push out their creativity and think of new ways of framing scenes. With so many shots from floor level or from Louis’ PoV, things could have got tiresome very quickly, but at just over five minutes in length, it never feels gimmicky or overstays its welcome.

Selected at festivals worldwide, Louis’ Shoes picked up the Gold medal in International Animation at the 2021 Student Academy Awards. Released online for a short period, as it’s hoping to be shortlisted for the Best Animated Short Film award at the 2022 Oscars, you should watch this charming little short while you can." - S/W Curator Rob Munday

title: Arbitrary | Gibberish Short Film | Siddhartha De Bose | Hook Films
description:

Finally, the film also speaks about gender roles - in cinema and in life.

title: Beyond | Award Winning Musical Short Film | Bhavadarshini | Hook Films
description:
The musical short film - 'Beyond' is way out of our daily life beliefs. What we see and trust cannot always be true. Not everyone has or share’s the same beliefs. Not everyone has the same experiences. But even if people do share the same experience you still may not view or believe in the same things. Because how we each endure and view an experience is based off of what we already think and believe. As individuals, we all have many beliefs. Some are more obvious and are usually similar to others. Those that are similar to others are more often not necessarily beliefs but are more similar to what we consider to be expected or normal. 
Life has already its challenges to overcome. Every human being is unique. Why try to categorize people when their true beauty lies in their differences? Who has the right to decide who or how to be beautiful?

Eri is always mollifying people with a fake smile on her face. One day, she turns into a doll with the same grin permanently frozen in place. No one notices, however, that she has transformed into a doll. Soon thereafter, she is discovered on the street by a talent scout, and she becomes a popular singing idol. A large number of people imitate Eri’s appearance, gradually taking on her fake smile over time. In order to change her situation, Eri takes real action for the first time in her life. title: Chasing The Storm (A Short Film)
description:
Chasing The Storm | A Short Film

Written by Takahiro Sugimura

Spring
In the sudden wind and momentary silence,
I give chase.

I try overlaying my heart onto the cloudy sky.
Swaying with the waves of emotion,
As if fleeing from my past self.

From the mundane everyday,
What lies ahead in the still unexplored, filled with curiosity?
Anxiety? Fear? Or perhaps, something joyful?

The suppressed air bursts forth,
Becoming a storm that approaches,
The rain conveying a sense of liberation.
I have finally arrived,
To the true self I've been searching for.

I will continue to shine amidst the storm,
Brightly.

Director/Writer/DP/Edit/Color/SE - Takahiro Sugimura

title: "Bazaar" - Persian Short Film
description:
When a young boy goes missing in the Tehran Bazaar, his mother assumes the worst. 

Bazaar was chosen to be screened at the 67th annual Berlin International Film Festival (Berlinale) as part of a short film screening. 

Bazaar was also featured in the San Marcos, Texas newspaper and screened twice at two Back to School festivals. 

This student short film was created for Bita Ghasemi's and Tess Cline's Narrative Production film class at the University of Texas at Austin. The task was to create a film without using dialogue to drive the narrative. The choice to use Persian without subtitling was intentional. 

Enjoy!

title: Summer Afternoon | Short Film | Kunal Ahuja
description:
Zervaan and Snehal are two lovestruck, old-school souls who rush into love after meeting just once at a movie theatre. In a world where lovers meet virtually and words have no meaning, they deep-dive into conversations surrounding the very nature of love and existence, drawing on various metaphors from their own environment. 
With champagne and heartbreaks, the film takes us through the beautiful journey of being together, as the romantic couple questions the meaning of love and identity, as they prepare for their unexpected, oncoming fate.

title: Pralhad | Award-winning Short Film| Ft. Ritwik Sahore | Schbang Motion Pictures
description:
Chronicling the inspiring first steps of a young 14-year-old boy in 1945 India who went on to build the Rs. 10000 crore Finolex Group from a humble 10-rupee note, “Pralhad” unveils a tale of great resolve and success through kindness. 

Based on true events from Late Shri Pralhad Chhabria’s autobiography ‘There’s No Such Thing as a Self-Made Man’, this period film follows a journey that sets the tone for the life and triumphs of this visionary leader, to the pinnacle of Indian manufacturing. 

Echoing the values of Finolex Group and its legacy to this day, “Pralhad” is an inspiration for every Indian entrepreneur starting out.

Watch the phenomenal story of Late Shri Pralhad Chhabria, Founder of Finolex Group.

"Overpopulation is the worst kind of pollution." 

When even basic survival has become a challenge nowadays with something as crucial as water also being a "Privilege", then how come we haven't questioned the one privilege that is always seen as a matter of a "personal" right- REPRODUCTION? We need to move from Plan Pregnancy to a Plan B, because humanity cannot move to a Planet B. 
"Mera Number kab aayega" is a dystopian tale set in 2030 where pregnancy requires government licenses, and couples seeking children only to resolve their personal conflicts require introspection.

title: This student short film got me into 10 film festivals (Shot on Fuji XT4)
description:

Instagram | http://instagram.com/sadiel_gomez

Description:

After a year and a half of waiting to make my short film "Ollie" available for the general public, the moment has arrived to finally share it with all of you. It's remarkable how this project began as a school assignment without putting much effort into the production, but later, when I sat down to edit and weave the narrative together, a wave of appreciation washed over me. I fell in love with the way I had told the story and the powerful message it carried.

Working with my dog Charlie as the main character proved to be a challenge of its own. It took countless hours to coax him into the right positions, and when I think back on this process, I appreciate the dedication required of any filmmaker working with animal actors. While I know there are areas that can be improved, I take immense pride in what I have accomplished as a solo filmmaker. The unexpected reception of "Ollie" at numerous film festivals has astounded me, serving as a testament to the notion that one can create something meaningful with minimal equipment and still garner recognition.

The journey of creating "Ollie" has been a profound learning experience, reinforcing the belief that anyone with passion and determination can produce a piece of cinema that resonates deeply. I am grateful for the opportunity to share this film with the general public, inviting them to witness the magic that unfolds when we embrace the power of storytelling, even in the most humble of circumstances.

Synopsis:

Ollie tells the story of the daily life of a dog at the beginning of the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic. The dog realizes that his human has stopped leaving the house for work in the morning. He feels extremely happy that his human stays in the house all day, every day with him. But one day, the human becomes very sick and suddenly is gone. The dog stays alone for many days without knowing if his human will return.

title: No Offense 🏆 Adult Animation Short Film - AWARD WINNING
description:
NO OFFENSE: An award winning 2D animated short film. A group of cartoonists are put on trial and the grim members of the jury sentence them to death. One of the artists refuses to accept his fate.
-
NO OFFENSE is an award-winning animated short film by Kris Borghs. The film received awards at film festivals including International Short Film Festival Leuven, Landshut Short Film Festival and European Short Film Festival of Bordeaux. No Offense is published with the permission of the filmmakers.
-
ABOUT SHORTFRAME: We curate a selection of award winning short films; the best short films direct from the film festival circuit. Whether it's Drama, Documentary, Horror, Sci-Fi or Comedy, Cannes, Berlin, Sundance or first time filmmakers: Short Frame is home to the best short films from the world’s most innovative filmmaking talent.
-
ABOUT THE FILM:  No Offence was created in response to the attack on Ali Farzat, a Syrian cartoonist whose hands were broken because of his critical portrayal of his president. While Kris Borghs was writing, designing and animating this film, other creators were less lucky: a Russian had to flee his country for painting Putin in lingerie, a French cartoonist was put on trial for insulting the pope, North Korea threatened war over a Kim Jong-Un persiflage and the tragic raid on Charlie Hebdo took the level of violence against artists to a terrifying new level. This clever and witty animation purposely questions the limitations on political free speech and creative expression in societies across the world.
-

© SOIL Productions - published with the permission of the filmmakers.

title: Dev Deepavali | Himalayan Fire Festival | Anoop Grover
description:
Dev Deepavali is a nine minute documentary film about a unique ‘Fire Festival’, celebrated in the quaint village of Tindar, Himachal Pradesh. 

Dev Deepavali, also known as Budhi (old) Diwali, is the continued celebration of biggest festival in India, only that it happens a month after Diwali celebrations are over everywhere. Villagers light up their mashaal (torches made of deodar and pine wood) and perform a dance.

Why is this festival celebrated a month late in pockets of Himachal Pradesh? Watch the film to know more! 

This year, Dev Deepavali will be celebrated on 24th November, 2022.

title: 23 B Raheja | One night. One truth. A lifetime of silence shattered. | Hindi Short Film
description:
23B Raheja is a gripping one-night drama that peels back the glossy layers of the entertainment industry to expose the shadows lurking beneath. The story revolves around a celebrated casting director whose charm masks a long trail of manipulation and exploitation.

His power begins to crumble when a young woman arrives at his door, posing as an aspiring actress—but with a haunting connection to his past. As the night unfolds, so does a tense game of revelations, where truth becomes confrontation and justice takes an unexpected form.

Taut, timely, and unsettlingly real, 23B Raheja is not just a story of reckoning—it’s a mirror held up to the systems we too often ignore.

title: Beginning | Friendship Day Special | Bengali Short Film | Arif Rahaman | Hook Films
description:
Friendship is like a new day, a new year, a new job, a new life, a new relationship, a new start—they all come to us without permission, in the best and worst way. They barge in our front doors with the beautiful promise of second chances and new potential and unexpected opportunity.
Life has no fixed beginning or end: arbitrarily one chooses that moment of experience from which to look back or from which to look ahead. Let's celebrate with Beginning on this #FriendshipDay, since friendship is one of the magical qualities that bring joy and enjoyment into life. Different to love, it can grow in to love, or it can become a whole special relationship of its own. A friend is someone who knows the song in your heart, and can sing it back to you when you have forgotten the words.

description:
Congratulations to James W Griffiths for his BAFTA award for Short Film for Room 8.

Room 8 is one of five different films from the same script: the Bombay Sapphire Imagination Series. Seeking to spark the imagination, we asked Oscar winning writer Geoffrey Fletcher to write a short script stripped of any stage direction. 
The five most imaginative film entries were picked, produced and premiered at Tribeca Film Festival 2013.

title: SWEEKAR | A Heart-Touching Marathi Short Film by Ravindra Satpute @vijaypatwardhanfoundation8434
description:
A young boy goes to the market with his father to buy toy warriors for their fort. Among all the perfect toys, he chooses the broken one. Watch the full film to know why?

Sweekar is a tender Marathi short film that beautifully captures the bond between a boy and his differently-abled father and it reminds us that even when something seems incomplete, it still holds immense value.

🎬 Written & Directed by: Ravindra Satpute  

💬 “Sometimes, acceptance is the truest form of love.”

If this story touched your heart, share it with your loved ones and tell us what it made you feel in the comments below.

समीर त्याच्या आईसारखा मसालेभात बनवण्याचा वारंवार प्रयत्न करतो. पण मसालेभाताला आईच्या हातची चव येत नाही. आईच्या आठवणी, भावना आणि जुन्या गोष्टी उलगडत असताना त्याला जाणवतं की काही पदार्थांची चव बनवणाऱ्याच्या हातात नसते तर ती कुटुंबासोबत टेबलवर शेअर केलेले प्रेम आणि क्षणांनी आपोआप येते, आणि शेवटी जेव्हा समीरला मसालेभात जमतो, तेव्हा चितळे डेरीच्या आम्रखंडासोबत सणाची गोडी पुन्हा एकदा कुटुंबाच्या टेबलवर परत येते.

title: David Bradley & Rachel Shenton star in this short film about finding unlikely friends
description:
Trapped in a lonely existence, reclusive widower Roy (BAFTA Winner David Bradley) passes the days by cold-calling strangers from the phone book, looking for brief moments of companionship. But when he accidentally calls adult hotline worker Cara (Rachel Shenton), an unlikely friendship is born that will help them both rediscover the joy of life. From the Academy Award®-Winning team behind The Silent Child, Roy is a funny, heart-warming tale of two lost souls who find companionship just when they need it most.

BAFTA 2022 shortlisted for Best British Short Film
WINNER Best Actor (Davd Bradley) at British Short Film Awards 2021
Official selection at  at Palm Springs Shortsfest 2021
Santa Barbara International Film Festival 2021 Flickerfest International Short Film Festival 2022

title: My New Neighbour | A Short Film by Katha Studios
description:
After moving into a new apartment, Meera finds herself drawn to her quiet and shy neighbour, Shaurya. Their interactions are limited to awkward hellos and brief encounters, while the familiar sounds of Shaurya’s parents fill Meera’s home with a sense of warmth and comfort.

As Meera slowly develops a crush on Shaurya, she tries to find a way to get closer to him. But when she finally enters his apartment, she discovers a truth she never expected.

What begins as a simple story of a new neighbour and an innocent crush quietly turns into a story about loneliness, grief and the unexpected comfort of knowing that someone is there for you.

A Katha Studios Film

title: ExMates |  Episode 5 | Sagar Veen, Sheena Chohan | Vibhav Ameta
description:
It’s Shreya’s birthday & she is a mess. She speaks with her Mama & breaks thenews of her break up with Kunal, who is trying to be nice with her today. Hemakes her coffee & offers it but Shreya is in no mood. She ignores, shuts thedoor on him & breaks down. She gets a call from Neha who tries to cheer &comfort her. It kind of works as Shreya changes into her birthday clothes,makes herself a cake, pours her a glass of wine & joins her zoom party with 4of her closest friends. After having a good time, she leaves her room & ismesmerized by what she sees – the look of the apartment has changed, Kunalhas put on some fairy lights & diyas, he has also left a glass of wine with abirthday note for Shreya. She finds this to be pretty sweet, she goes up toKunal & pours him a glass and asks him to join her.

title: Tumhare Bina | Award Winning Short Film | Shailendra Kumar Jha
description:
‘Tumhare Bina" (Without You) a film set in the time of pandemic and lockdown, is as much about
love and longing as it is about isolation and loneliness. Premier of the film happened at the WOIS Film Festival, Dubai on 9th December 2021.
Since then it has garnered critical acclaim across film festivals around the world.
Official Selection, Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival
Official Selection, Bengaluru International Short Film Festival
Winner, Best Indian Director, Pune Short Film Festival
Official Selection, Minikino Film Week, Bali International Short Film Festival
Official Selection, South Asian Short Film Festival
Official Selection, Bengal International Short Film Festival
Critics Choice Award, International Short Film, Druk International Film Festival, Bhutan
Critics Choice Award, Debut Filmmaker, Tagore International Short Film Festival
Winner, Best Short Script/Screenplay, Indo French International Film Festival
Winner, Special Mention Award for Best Indian Short Film, Indo French International Short Film
Official Selection, Kerala Short Film Festival
Finalist, Tokyo International Short Film Festival

An elderly man, Amitabh is forced to live and handle the grief alone after the death of his wife. His children, who live in cities far away, are unable to visit till the pandemic related travel restrictions are eased. Amitabh is confronted with overwhelming emptiness and troubles with sleep. He and his wife had barely been apart since their marriage and he is used to her being around, at home and in bed. When even sleeping pills don’t do the job, Amitabh works out an extra-ordinary solution that runs the risk of him being laughed and sniggered at or as his daughter bluntly puts it – being called a Pervert!

title: Tangdi | Short Film | Sourabh Supnekar
description:
In a world where civilized mannerisms don’t exist two roommates have a constant need of 
eating meat. Similar to our world a lockdown is announced in their world. Their daily supply of 
meat is cut off and hence they try everything in their power to get their hands on it. But as every shop and hotel is closed and civilized mannerisms don’t exist they don’t get meat nor does anyone help them. They try to cook the meat themselves but fail. They have access to basic food but they are pining away to eat meat. This leads to a heated situation between them and one of them goes to find meat alone. He miraculously gets his hands on a plate of chicken tangdi. He comes back to the room thinking that the roommate might be out, but that’s not the case. He does not want to 
share the meat and hence is trying to avoid the roommate. The roommate notices the meat but he runs away. The roommate chases him following the smell of the meat. He finally runs on to a street where a beggar is sitting. Disregarding the beggar, he starts eating but before he can even take a bite the roommate arrives and they start fighting on the road. The plate of meat falls on the road. The beggar walks up to them picks up the piece of meat and stares at them.

title: Framed | Short Film | Jose Jacob | Hook Films
description:
Framed is about a person stuck inside a space unknown to him and his discovery of what that space is and his struggle to escape from that space. The world of film is always built with a rectangular box, which we accept as our scope of view - and it is this basic psychology that helps us tell any story using the language of cinema. But what if that view itself feels restrictive? A meta investigation of the same is carried out with the film- Framed. And this frame can also be a metaphorical restriction of any aspect of life and is kept open for interpretation- The filmmaker's understanding of his or her film stops mattering the moment the product is shown to an audience, at least that is what he or believe, so it's the up-to-the audience to watch and interpret according to your experience of watching it.

description:
Short film based on the situation after the judgment of Indian Supreme Court on IPC Section 377 to re-criminalize the homosexuality on December 2013. KHAROSROTA goes with the name Torsha, a hilly river of West Bengal; which is both speedy and wild in nature. But her story is not reachable to everyone as so many barriers and dangers are there at source of the river. Even then she flows beyond all the hurdles to reach her destiny. In this story Rumi introduced Torsha to Apu and suddenly their life get completely transformed. Overwhelmed hearts touching love story, which will make you feel something different beyond the usual Indian society thinking.
